    - id: FR-MCP-141
      title: Service-account process environment fidelity
      body: When the server runs as a Windows service under a non-interactive account, child processes it launches shall resolve executables and environment the same way an interactive user session would. Executable resolution shall skip Microsoft\WindowsApps App-Execution-Alias stubs, which are zero-byte reparse points that fail with Win32Exception 1920 for service accounts. Tunnel providers shall apply the interactive user's USERPROFILE, HOME, APPDATA, and PATH to the child process so provider configuration files resolve, and shall resolve the provider binary against that enriched PATH. A missing provider binary shall be reported at Warning with a message naming the service-account and Store-alias causes and the available remedies, not as an unexplained error.       title: Session-log turns persist without a title and never lose a refined one
      body: A session-log turn shall persist end to end when its title is deliberately omitted, and a title the agent has refined shall never be overwritten by a stale local copy. Thirteen open triage reports (BUG-TRIAGE-086 through 101, excluding the already-closed 097) collapse into five root causes, of which two account for eleven of the reports. First, the plugin PowerShell core rejects an empty title at parameter binding even though TR-MCP-REPL-015 requires callers to omit the title so a stale cached one is not resubmitted, so appendDialog, appendActions, completeTurn and the supersede path all fail. Second, the typed client posts anonymous request bodies through a source-generated JSON context that has no metadata for compiler-generated types, so the dedicated retitle endpoints throw before reaching the server. The remaining three are the supersede path clobbering a server-refined title from the local cache, failTurn refusing to close a turn the plugin cache shows as active, and a storage outage leaving health reporting Healthy while every persistence call fails behind inconsistent error shapes.

    - id: FR-MCP-HVPIPE-003
      title: 'Reviewer readiness: NONCE, offline, and online'
      body: 'Reviewer readiness: NONCE, offline, and online. Sources: S-15, S-27, P-04, R-10, R-24. Use cases: UC-HV-02.'
      workspaceId: /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer
      priority: high
      status: pending
      notes: Proposed in architecture Amendment 1 (docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md, section 19.1); plan PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001, not approved; created 2026-10-16 so the requirement is captured as it emerges.
      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: Given an `Offline` reviewer, when nothing but an execution or a configuration change happens, then it never becomes `Online`; only a passing probe makes it `Online` (`ReviewerBecomesOnlineOnlyByPassingProbe`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given a probe whose log echoes the run's nonce, whose provenance names the expected model and effort, and whose reviewer turn exists, of a reviewer that is `Unverified` or `Offline` with an open incident, when it closes, then the reviewer is `Online` with the resolved model and effort, `ReadinessChangedUtc` set, `LastProbeRunId` naming the run, `ReadinessReason` and `OpenIncidentId` cleared while the incident row stays, and `reviewer_online` is appended (`ProbePassedReviewerOnlineResolvedModelAndEffort`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given a probe with a wrong nonce, missing or different provenance, or no reviewer turn, when it closes, then the reviewer is `Offline` with `probe_nonce_mismatch`, `runtime_identity_mismatch`, or `reviewer_turn_logging_unsupported` and an incident is `Pending` (`ProbeFailuresOfflineWithCodeAndIncident`); given a probe whose stored chunks fail V-1, then the run is `Failed` with `evidence_corrupt`, an incident `hv-server-evidence_corrupt` is `Pending`, the reviewer's readiness is unchanged, and no probe is requested again (`ProbeEvidenceCorruptServerIncidentReadinessUnchanged`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given a probe already requested or running, when another NONCE is requested, then 202 `AlreadyRequested` or `Running` and no second probe exists (`NonceRepeatNoSecondProbe`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given a disabled reviewer, when a NONCE is requested, then 409 `hv_reviewer_disabled` (`NonceDisabledReviewer409`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: Given enabled `Unverified` reviewers at startup, when the worker starts, then a probe is requested for each and none for a disabled or `Offline` reviewer, and a startup request refused with 503 `audit_unavailable` is made again at the next iteration, and not again once its reviewer is disabled (409 `hv_reviewer_disabled`) (`WorkerStartupProbesUnverifiedEnabledReviewersOnly`); given an `Unverified` reviewer whose probe of its current configuration settled on a server fault (`evidence_corrupt`), when the worker restarts, then no probe is requested until a caller asks (`WorkerRestartNeverRetriesSettledProbe`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: "Given a probe running for configuration version 1 and an update that makes it version 2, when the old probe closes with a passing answer, then its run is `Failed` with `probe_stale_configuration`, the reviewer stays `Unverified` with its new probe request, and only a probe of version 2 can make it `Online` (H3: `StaleProbeNeverQualifiesNewConfiguration`); given instead that the old probe fails to launch, exits nonzero, ends `worker_shutdown`, or has its lease expire after the update, then the reviewer's readiness, reason, probe request, and open incident are unchanged, no reviewer incident is filed, and no probe of version 1 is requested (H3: `StaleProbeFailureShutdownOrExpiryLeavesNewConfigurationUnchanged`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: "Given a probe of the reviewer's current configuration whose launch fails or whose process exits nonzero, when FailHvRunCommand records it, then the reviewer is `Offline` with the code and an incident and no request state is written; given a probe ended by `worker_shutdown`, then no incident exists, the reviewer is unchanged, and the probe is requested again (H3: `ProbeFailureOfflineWithIncidentAndShutdownRequestsProbeAgain`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1

    - id: FR-MCP-HVPIPE-007
      title: 'Durable scheduling: queue, leases, fences, and restart safety'
      body: 'Durable scheduling: queue, leases, fences, and restart safety. Sources: S-17, S-24, handoff requirement 10, R-07, R-13. Use cases: UC-HV-04, UC-HV-09.'
      workspaceId: /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer
      priority: high
      status: pending
      notes: Proposed in architecture Amendment 1 (docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md, section 19.1); plan PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001, not approved; created 2026-10-16 so the requirement is captured as it emerges.
      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: Given a submission, when it commits, then the worker is woken and claims it without a manual trigger, and when the wake-up is lost (a crash after the commit, W-01) the next poll claims it (`SubmitWakesWorkerAutoStart`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given two workers claiming at once, when both run, then exactly one run is claimed per request, on three providers (W-11, `ClaimConcurrentWorkersOneRunPerRequestThreeProviders`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given a run whose lease expired before its process started, while it ran, or after its process exited but before its close committed (W-02, W-03, W-04), when the sweep runs, then the run is `Abandoned`, its fence token is incremented, its output stays stored as evidence (L-02), and the request is `Queued` with attempts left; on its last counted attempt it is `Failed`, and with a cancel requested it is `Canceled`, each ended request with its turns `None`, its `Pending` responses `Closed` with `request_ended`, and `hv_failed` or `hv_canceled` appended, exactly as after FailHvRunCommand (`LeaseExpiryAbandonsFencesAndRequeues`, `LeaseExpiryEndsRequestLikeFailedRun`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given a worker whose lease was taken over, when it records its start, appends, heartbeats, closes, or fails, then each answers `stale_fence` and nothing changes (`StaleFenceEveryWorkerWriteRefusedNothingChanged`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given a request `Finalizing` when the server restarted (W-05), when the sweep runs, then FinalizeHvRequestCommand finalizes it once (`SweepFinalizesFinalizingRequestOnce`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: Given a graceful shutdown during a run, when the worker stops, then the run ends `worker_shutdown`, no incident exists, the reviewer is unchanged, and the attempt is not counted (`GracefulShutdownNotCountedNoIncident`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: Given two registered workspaces, each with queued requests, when each workspace's worker claims, then no run or request crosses workspaces (`WorkerClaimsOnlyItsWorkspace`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: 'Given a reviewer that has started a descendant, when its worker process is killed abruptly, then the reviewer and every descendant end without any call by the dead worker and without a time limit, and after the lease expires the request is queued again (H3, a scripted fake reviewer and a worker process the test kills: `WorkerDeathEndsReviewerTreeAndRequeues`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC009
        text: 'Given a claimed run, when its process starts, then RecordHvRunStartCommand makes it `Running` with `StartedUtc` and `ProcessId` before the `hv_brief` append; given a crash between the process start and that commit, then the run stays `Claimed`, the reviewer ends with its worker, and the lease expiry queues a new attempt; given RecordHvRunStartCommand or RecordHvRunHeartbeatCommand answered with a retryable `conflict`, then the worker repeats the same call, and a repeated start with the same process id after its commit returns the stored start and writes nothing (H3: `RunStartRecordedBeforeBriefAndCrashRecovered`, `RunStartAndHeartbeatRetryableConflictRepeated`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC010
        text: "Given two sweeps that both read run R of a request as expired, the first abandoning R and requeuing the request, and a new run of that request claimed before the second sweep's transaction, when the second sweep runs, then FencedLease `Expire` skips R, R is abandoned once with one server incident, the request keeps its new run and stays `Running`, and policy HvRetryDecision was applied once (H3: `SecondSweepSkipsRunAlreadyTakenOver`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC011
        text: 'Given a run abandoned by one sweep and a later run of the same request finalized `Completed`, when a second sweep that had read the first run as expired runs, then the request stays `Completed` with its result, no turn is released, and neither `hv_failed` nor `hv_canceled` is appended (H7: `LateSweepNeverRevivesCompletedRequest`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1
    - id: FR-MCP-HVPIPE-008
      title: 'Execution lifecycle: true live output, heartbeats, no time limit, cancellation'
      body: 'Execution lifecycle: true live output, heartbeats, no time limit, cancellation. Sources: S-18, S-22, P-02, R-11, R-12, R-28. Use cases: UC-HV-04, UC-HV-08.'
      workspaceId: /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer
      priority: high
      status: pending
      notes: Proposed in architecture Amendment 1 (docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md, section 19.1); plan PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001, not approved; created 2026-10-16 so the requirement is captured as it emerges.
      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: 'Given a reviewer that writes lines over time, including a single line followed by silence, when it runs, then every line is appended within `OutputFlushInterval` of being written, in order, whether or not another line arrives (H3: `OutputLinesAppendedWithinFlushIntervalInOrder`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given a buffer reaching `OutputFlushBytes`, when the next line arrives, then the buffer is appended at once (`OutputFlushedAtByteThreshold`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given a scripted fake reviewer that writes one line and then blocks on a gate the test controls, when the test reads the run's output stream, then the line arrives while the gate is closed and the process is still running (operator-confirmed P8, `LiveOutputLineObservableBeforeReviewerExits`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given a reviewer running longer than any interval the configuration names, when nothing else happens, then no unit or process ends it (`ReviewerRunHasNoTimeLimit`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given a `Queued` request, when canceled, then it is `Canceled`, its turns are `None`, and `hv_canceled` is appended; given a `Running` request, then it becomes `CancelRequested`, and at the next heartbeat the process is stopped and the request is `Canceled` (`CancelQueuedImmediateRunningAtNextHeartbeat`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: Given a cancel racing a finalization, a claim, or a close of one request (W-10), when both run, then exactly one commits and the other sees its state, on three providers (`CancelVersusFinalizeOneCommitsThreeProviders`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: Given a `Finalizing`, `Completed`, or `Failed` request, when canceled, then 409 `hv_request_not_cancelable` (`CancelTerminalOrFinalizing409`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: "Given an interactive session of a reviewer's agent live in the workspace, when a review run and a probe run of that reviewer start and end, then the interactive session's plugin state files and its session-log session are byte-for-byte unchanged, and the reviewer's turn is in a session of its own (H1 Pester per plugin host, and the live check: `ReviewerRunLeavesSameAgentLiveSessionUnchanged`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC009
        text: "Given each adapter's launch and a reviewer told to create or change a workspace file, when the run ends, then the attempt was refused or the tool was never offered, and the workspace tree outside the plugin's own host-session state is unchanged (H1, per adapter, with the probe streams of 2026-10-16 as fixtures: `ReviewerRunCannotChangeWorkspaceFilesPerAdapter`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC010
        text: "Given a server-launched reviewer whose host enforces the foundation's Stop gate, when it has emitted its verdict record, then its own `Chore` turn is closed through the completion gate and the process exits on its own, never held open by the gate (H1 Pester per host and the live check: `ReviewerClosesOwnTurnAndExitsUnderStopGate`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC011
        text: "Given a scripted fake reviewer that starts a child process which keeps the reviewer's output pipes open, when its run is canceled, its fence goes stale, or the ledger fails, and also when the reviewer's root process exits on its own first, then the reviewer and every descendant are ended, the output is read to its end, and the attempt ends with no process left running (H3: `ReviewerStopEndsWholeProcessTree`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC012
        text: "Given a cancel that commits after the run's last heartbeat and before its process exits with code 0, when CloseHvRunOutputCommand runs, then the run is `Canceled`, the request is `Canceled` with its turns released and `hv_canceled` appended, and no finalization starts; a repeat cancel of a `CancelRequested` or `Canceled` request returns 200 unchanged, on three providers (H3: `CancelCommittedBeforeCloseWinsOverFinalizing`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1
    - id: FR-MCP-HVPIPE-009
      title: 'Execution failures: incidents through triage, offline, retry bound'
      body: 'Execution failures: incidents through triage, offline, retry bound. Sources: S-15, S-26, R-17. Use cases: UC-HV-09.'
      workspaceId: /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer
      priority: high
      status: pending
      notes: Proposed in architecture Amendment 1 (docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md, section 19.1); plan PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001, not approved; created 2026-10-16 so the requirement is captured as it emerges.
      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: Given a reviewer-attributable failure, when recorded, then the reviewer is `Offline` with the code and incident, and an incident is `Pending` with `dedupeKey` `hv-reviewer-<reviewerId>-<code>` (`ReviewerFailureOfflineWithIncident`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given a pending incident, when filed, then the triage service receives its `dedupeKey` and the incident records the report and group ids (`IncidentFiledThroughTriageWithDedupeKey`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given the same failure twice, or one filing retried after triage accepted it but before its report id was recorded (W-09, L-03), when both are filed, then triage groups them in one group (`RepeatedFailureSameTriageGroup`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given triage unreachable, or a crash after the incident committed and before its filing (W-08), when filing, then the incident stays `Pending` with the error and the next sweep files it (`IncidentFilingRetriedUntilFiled`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given attempts spent, when the last attempt fails, then the request is `Failed` with `attempts_exhausted`, its turns are `None`, and `hv_failed` is appended (`AttemptsExhaustedRequestFailedTurnsReleased`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: Given a server-attributable failure (`evidence_corrupt`, `snapshot_changed`, `model_grade_conflict`, `reviewer_not_independent`), when recorded, then an incident with `hv-server-<code>` exists and the reviewer is unchanged (`ServerFailureIncidentReviewerUnchanged`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: 'Given an unwritable ledger, when an incident is filed, then the triage service is never called and the incident stays `Pending`; given a ledger that fails after triage accepted, then the incident stays `Pending` and the retry joins the same triage group; given a filing that succeeds, then `Filed` and `incident_filed` commit in one transaction (H3: `IncidentFilingNeverCallsTriageWhileLedgerUnavailable`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: "Given a worker FailHvRunCommand (for a corrupt brief, a launch failure, a cancel, a corrupt append, or a nonzero exit) answered 503 `audit_unavailable` or `stale_fence`, when the worker handles it (FailAttempt), then the attempt ends with no further write, the request's status and version are unchanged, and the lease expiry later recovers the run; given one answered with a retryable `conflict`, then the same call is repeated; given FileHvIncidentCommand answered 503 `audit_unavailable` at the sweep, then the worker host claims nothing in that iteration (H3: `FailAttemptRefusalEndsAttemptWithoutStateClaim`, `WorkerIterationStopsWhenIncidentFilingAuditUnavailable`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1

      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: Given a log with one assessment per member, one holistic record, and one verdict record last, when finalized, then each requested turn has its score, the holistic evaluation is stored separately, and the run's `VerdictRecordSha256` is the SHA-256 of the verdict record in its stored normal form (`FinalizeStoresPerTurnScoresAndSeparateHolistic`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given a log missing an assessment, with two verdict records, without a holistic record, or with a finding without remediation, when finalized, then `reviewer_output_invalid` and nothing is committed (`FinalizeIncompleteOutputRefusedNothingCommitted`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given a holistic correctness of 0.97 with every turn AGREE, when finalized, then the overall verdict is DISAGREE (`OverallVerdictHolisticBelow098Disagree`); given an AGREE verdict with a FAIL finding, then `reviewer_output_invalid` (`VerdictAgreeWithFailFindingRefused`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given turn scores whose mean differs from the holistic scores, when finalized, then the stored holistic scores are the reviewer's own, never recomputed (`HolisticScoresNeverComputedFromTurnScores`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given a record the reviewer forged as `hv_provenance` or `hv_brief` inside its message text, when the log is read, then it is not accepted as a worker record (`ForgedWorkerRecordInMessageTextIgnored`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: Given native streams of each CLI, recorded from the probe runs of 2026-10-16, in which a record is split across events (Grok's per-token text), repeated in a delta and in the whole message (Copilot), inside a fenced block, or beside other text on its line, when the records are extracted as the lines arrive and again over the stored log, then each record is extracted exactly once, the line with other text is free text, and both extractions return the same records (`ReviewerRecordsExtractedOnceFromAssembledMessagesPerCli`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: 'Given a run that exits with code 0 and holds no reviewer records (an empty output, or a stream its CLI ended `cancelled`), when it closes, then a review fails with `reviewer_output_invalid`, the reviewer is `Offline` with an incident, and a probe fails with `probe_nonce_mismatch`; an exit code never stands in for a verdict (H7, where V-8 refuses the review: `ExitZeroWithoutReviewerRecordsIsNotAReview`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: "Given a reviewer turn that holds only the `hv_verdict` record, one that is still `in_progress`, one closed `failed`, one not classified `Chore`, or one created before the run's claim, when the request finalizes, then V-6 refuses each with `reviewer_turn_unverified`; given a completed `Chore` turn holding every reviewer record of the run in order, then V-6 passes (H7: `ReviewerTurnMustBeCompletedChoreHoldingEveryRecord`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC009
        text: 'Given an AGREE holistic verdict at 0.99 and every turn AGREE, but one response grade DISAGREE, or one response finding UNKNOWN, when finalized, then the overall verdict is DISAGREE, and a reviewer that reported AGREE there is refused by V-4 with `reviewer_output_invalid` (H7: `OverallVerdictOnePredicateOverTurnsHolisticResponsesFindings`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC010
        text: "Given an admitted response whose grade is a score-only DISAGREE (scores below 0.98, every claim finding PASS) and whose response is rejected or superseded before V-4 reads it, or after V-4 and before the commit, with every other verdict AGREE, when finalized, then V-4 accepts the reviewer's overall DISAGREE, the stored overall verdict is DISAGREE, and no model grade is applied to the closed response (H7: `OverallVerdictBindsAdmittedResponsesNotLaterState`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1
    - id: FR-MCP-HVPIPE-011
      title: Evidence completeness, GZIP at rest, round-trip verification
      body: 'Evidence completeness, GZIP at rest, round-trip verification. Sources: S-13, S-30, R-12, R-14. Use cases: UC-HV-04, UC-HV-05, UC-HV-10.'
      workspaceId: /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer
      priority: high
      status: pending
      notes: Proposed in architecture Amendment 1 (docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md, section 19.1); plan PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001, not approved; created 2026-10-16 so the requirement is captured as it emerges.
      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: Given an accepted request and a run's lines, when stored, then every payload is a GZIP member that decompresses to the exact bytes, and no uncompressed copy is stored (`EvidenceStoredGzipOnlyRoundTripExact`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given a chunk whose bytes, SHA-256, or chain hash was altered, or a missing sequence, when finalized, then `evidence_corrupt` and nothing is committed (`FinalizeCorruptOrTruncatedLogRefused`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given a compression whose round trip fails, when admitted or appended, then 500 `evidence_corrupt` and nothing is saved (`CompressionRoundTripFailureNothingSaved`); for an append (the sequence 1 `hv_brief` append, a flush, or the final flush), and for one answered with a non-retryable `conflict` or a 400 `validation_error`, the worker appends no later sequence, stops the reviewer and fails the run with `evidence_corrupt`, so an incident `hv-server-evidence_corrupt` is `Pending`, the reviewer is unchanged, and the request goes through policy HvRetryDecision (`AppendEvidenceCorruptFailsRunAsServerFault`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given a finalized run, when the response log is downloaded compressed and read back as one GZIP stream (VI-07), then decompression yields every stored line in order and its SHA-256 chain equals the run's (`ResponseLogDownloadMultiMemberGzipMatchesChain`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given a reviewer output of any size, when appended, then no limit truncates it (`OutputHasNoSizeLimitNeverTruncated`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: "Given a finalized request, when its `Result` evidence is read back, then the stored payload holds no `evidence.result` digest, its SHA-256 equals `ResultSha256`, and the returned document's `evidence.result.sha256` equals that value (H7: `ResultEvidenceDigestExcludesItselfAndRoundTrips`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: "Given a result document whose compression fails its round trip inside the finalization transaction, when finalized, then the transaction rolls back and nothing of the result is visible, and the run fails with `evidence_corrupt` as a server fault (an incident `hv-server-evidence_corrupt`, the reviewer unchanged) through policy HvRetryDecision, so the request's attempts bound the retries (H7: `ResultCompressionFailureFailsRunAsServerFault`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: 'Given a stored payload that fails to decompress, when GetHvRequestQuery returns its last output (directly or for a SubmitHvRequestCommand replay), GetHvResultQuery assembles the result, GetHvEvidenceQuery decompresses it, or the output stream sends it, then the read is recorded first, each query and the replay answer HTTP 500 with code `evidence_corrupt` before their first byte or end their body incomplete after it, and the stream sends the event `hv_stream_error` whose data field `code` is `evidence_corrupt` and ends (H6: `CorruptStoredPayloadReadAnswersEvidenceCorrupt`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC009
        text: "Given a claimed review run whose `Request` evidence fails to decompress, when the worker builds its brief, then the read is recorded first, no reviewer process starts, and the run fails with `evidence_corrupt` as a server fault (an incident `hv-server-evidence_corrupt`, the reviewer unchanged) through policy HvRetryDecision, so the request's attempts bound the retries (H3: `CorruptRequestEvidenceAtBriefFailsRunAsServerFault`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1
    - id: FR-MCP-HVPIPE-012
      title: Atomic finalization and turn finality
      body: 'Atomic finalization and turn finality. Sources: S-06, S-07, S-23, R-04, R-15. Use cases: UC-HV-05, UC-HV-12.'
      workspaceId: /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer
      priority: high
      status: pending
      notes: Proposed in architecture Amendment 1 (docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture-Amendment-1-Durable-HV.md, section 19.1); plan PLAN-HVPIPELINE-001, not approved; created 2026-10-16 so the requirement is captured as it emerges.
      acceptanceCriteria:
      - id: AC001
        text: Given a fault injected after each write of CommitFinalResult (W-06), when finalization runs, then nothing of the result is visible after the rollback, the request stays `Finalizing`, and the next sweep finalizes it, on three providers (`FinalizeFaultAfterEachWriteNothingVisibleThreeProviders`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC002
        text: Given an admitted turn, when any turn write, review write, review reset, section write, dialog append, title change, or session replace or delete targets it from any origin but `HvFinalization`, then 409 `turn_immutable` with `hv_pending`, and after finalization with `hv_final` (`FrozenTurnEveryWritePathRefused`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC003
        text: Given a canceled or failed request, when it ends, then its turns are writable again (`EndedRequestReleasesTurns`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC004
        text: Given a request finalized, when FinalizeHvRequestCommand runs again, then it returns the stored outcome and writes nothing (`FinalizeTwiceSecondReturnsStoredNothingWritten`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC005
        text: Given a member turn changed by a path that bypasses the guard (a fixture writing the store directly), when finalized, then V-2 refuses with `snapshot_changed` (`FinalizeSnapshotChangedRefused`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC006
        text: Given a `Code` turn completed with hostile review `Other` "HV requested", when its HV finalizes, then its hostile review holds the HV result and its status stays `completed` (`FinalizeReplacesOtherPendingHvReviewKeepsStatus`).
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC007
        text: 'Given turns whose hostile review is `Pass` or `Fail`, `Other`, or absent when the A-11 migration adds the HV columns, when the migration runs, then exactly the `Pass` and `Fail` turns are `Final` with no request id, every write to them is refused with 409 `turn_immutable` `hv_final`, and an HV over them is refused with 409 `hv_turns_already_reviewed`, on three providers (the migration is built in HvStorageSchema; the criterion binds in H2, where the write guard and admission exist: `MigrationMarksHvReviewedTurnsFinalThreeProviders`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC008
        text: "Given two finalizers of one request, one committing the result and one whose verification failed on reads taken before that commit, when both run, then the request stays `Completed` with its result and the failing finalizer's FailHvRunCommand changes nothing and returns `already_completed`, on three providers (H7: `LateVerificationFailureCannotUndoCommittedFinalization`)."
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC009
        text: 'Given a verification failure whose FailHvRunCommand returns 503 `audit_unavailable`, 409 `conflict`, `stale_fence`, `not_finalizable`, or `already_completed`, when FinalizeHvRequestCommand reports, then it returns that outcome (`stale_fence` as `not_finalizable`), the request stays as FailHvRunCommand left it (`Finalizing` for a refusal), the worker reports that state, and the next sweep finalizes it; given a request whose state changed between the reads and the commit, then the unit starts again from its status check (H7: `FinalizerPropagatesEveryFailRunOutcome`).'
        isSatisfied: false
      scopeStartLayerKey: layer-1

    - id: FR-MCP-MARKER-004
      title: Marker removal deletes the marker and leaves no tombstone
      body: 'Removing the AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml workspace marker must delete the file. It must not rename the marker to an AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml.deleted-{timestamp} archive copy that is never reclaimed. The marker is regenerated in full on every server start and carries the per-workspace API key that rotates on each restart, so an archived copy preserves no recoverable state of value while leaving an expired credential on disk. Each graceful shutdown currently leaves one tombstone permanently: as of 2026-07-20 the QBrainAi workspace held 19 of them, 587,033 bytes, dated 2026-07-08 through 2026-07-16, every one containing the apiKey that was live when it was written. TR-MCP-DB-003 (soft deletes for persistent MCP data) governs persistent MCP domain rows and their relationships; it does not extend to regenerated filesystem artifacts, and applying it to the marker was an over-generalization. The same rule applies to the legacy .mcp-server.yaml and .mcp-server.json markers removed alongside it.'

      status: pending

      title: Built-in, non-disableable plugin
      body: >-
        ### FR-QB-001 (New): Built-in, non-disableable plugin

        TR-QB-PLUGIN-001 (New): Construct the pinned plugin through a protected integration adapter outside optional discovery/filtering. Bundle required assets, avoid duplicate SDK runtimes/dependency cycles, and reserve required contribution identities.

        - AC-QB-001: Startup automatically registers required tools, skills, and lifecycle capabilities without install/enablement prompts. TEST-QB-001: registers_bundled_plugin_without_user_enablement. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-002: Settings, flags, environment variables, tool filters, and same-name optional contributions cannot disable/replace required capabilities. The named test covers every enumerated bypass surface, optional hook input rewrites and provider-executed tools: only final authorized arguments execute; an adapter with unobservable execution is rejected unless tool execution is verifiably disabled. TEST-QB-002: rejects_required_plugin_disable_and_shadow_attempts. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-003: Missing, incompatible, incomplete, or invalid plugin assets block ordinary execution before the first model request. Pin, signed ClineQb entry, asset digest and host-platform compatibility must agree. Missing runtime prerequisites for a non-triggered skill do not block unrelated work; triggering that skill without its prerequisite blocks that workflow with an actionable diagnostic. TEST-QB-003: blocks_execution_when_required_plugin_is_unusable. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-068: Compiled desktop normal and configured-proxy startup use the selected cline-qb state and hub namespace, ignoring inherited upstream CLINE_* overrides. Executable validation uses a distinct temporary home, private state/discovery paths and OS-assigned ports, inherits no operator provider/account credentials, and cannot read or modify the operator home or attach to an operator hub. Seeded upstream canaries remain byte-identical with no new files after either readiness or a blocked startup. Missing trusted runtime identity blocks before publishing readiness; it is not accepted as a successful startup. Both positive readiness cases remain required once reviewed signed runtime dependencies are available. TEST-QB-068: isolates_compiled_startup_and_ignores_upstream_overrides. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-070: For the approved PowerShell shared-core contract, an ordinary governed launch on a clean supported host works using the pinned, verified runtime and every mandatory startup module/asset supplied by the artifact, without a user module cache, startup installation or runtime download. Runtime, module, host-interface and platform compatibility are checked together before readiness. Missing, incompatible or shadowed prerequisites give an actionable blocked state without an ungoverned fallback. Preserve the agreed C1-C12 observable behavior through migration. P1 proves the integration on its available execution host; P5 verifies every declared package target using the existing executed-versus-static-only matrix and its honest limitations. TEST cases: Empty module cache and no network; incompatible pwsh/module/REPL versions; wrong architecture; PATH or module shadow; omitted YAML or PowerShell.MCP dependency; supported diagnostic recovery; clean packaged launch; all required target builds present. TEST-QB-070: verifies_complete_pinned_powershell_runtime_offline. TDD: P1. Staged regressions: P5.

      title: Trusted, workspace-bound startup
      body: >-
        ### FR-QB-002 (New): Trusted, workspace-bound startup

        TR-QB-TRUST-001 (New): Resolve trust/routing from actual workspace; isolate contexts instead of process-global session state; maintain guidance in provider requests.

        - AC-QB-004: Signature/nonce/health/auth failures block ordinary execution without unauthorized further probing or ungoverned fallback. TEST-QB-004: fails_closed_on_workspace_trust_failure. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-005: Concurrent workspaces/sessions retain separate endpoints, credentials, session linkage, and request IDs. Steering, delayed callbacks, replay, resume and clear/end preserve the captured workspace, agent, MCP session, request and event attribution. With multiple delivered open turns an implicit write is request_ambiguous; a foreign request is request_unknown. A mint-only request is not an implicit write target; explicit valid targeting still works without canceling another open turn. TEST-QB-005: isolates_concurrent_workspace_and_session_contexts. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-006: Required skills/guidance precede work and survive requests/compaction; unavailable guidance is not false successful emptiness. Assert the complete pinned skill inventory, memory descriptor output and effective requirements in actual provider requests after prompt replacement, rebuild and compaction; successful empty memory alone permits None. Marker/bootstrap prompt text is absent, and unrelated skills do not execute automatically. TEST-QB-006: preserves_required_guidance_and_rejects_false_empty_results. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-072: At each ordinary execution and completion authorization boundary, a live context whose relevant signed trust, credentials, artifact authorization or policy has changed cannot authorize new work using its previous validation. It must revalidate the applicable current state or block with supported recovery. In-flight effects and late callbacks retain their original attribution and cannot mark a replacement context ready. Recovery retains the original audit records and cannot silently rebind them to another identity. An unaffected concurrent context continues normally. Supported changes, detection boundaries and in-flight outcome rules must be specified by the slice contract before implementation. TEST cases: Marker/key/policy change between initialization and tool execution; change between verification and completion; change while a tool is already executing; delayed response from old context; failed revalidation; unrelated concurrent workspace; restart with an old outbox. TEST-QB-072: invalidates_live_authorization_after_trust_or_policy_change. TDD: P1.

    - id: FR-QB-003
      title: Durable session auditing
      body: >-
        ### FR-QB-003 (New): Durable session auditing

        TR-QB-AUDIT-001 (New): Use supported plugin lifecycle/action/decision/persistence/recovery interfaces; keep decisions distinct from actions.

        - AC-QB-007: Every actual user request opens a linked turn with the full request text before agent work, using a deterministic provisional title derived from the request that is never empty and never the literal User prompt; before completion the turn carries a summary title meeting completion obligation (d). TEST-QB-007: opens_linked_request_turn_before_agent_work. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-008: Outcomes/errors/cancellation/decisions retain status, ordering, and separate action/decision classification. tool_execution is emitted only after the server/REPL/plugin taxonomy prerequisite is verified. One explicit decision has the same identity and conclusion in designDecisions, decision dialog and design_decision action after replay; tool activity alone does not invent a decision. Out-of-order acknowledgments cannot reorder stored events or transfer a canceled/terminal turn outcome to another request. TEST-QB-008: records_ordered_actions_and_separate_decisions. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-009: Pending/synthetic acknowledgments are not confirmed persistence; recovery retains records and avoids duplicate application. Crash/restart at capture, pending-to-minted rebinding, submission, server commit, receipt handling and retirement retains immutable event identity, payload and per-turn order. At-least-once replay applies one logical event and never changes its request attribution. Confirmed and verified-unchanged receipts require matching root identities, event/payload and positive committed revision; duplicate requestIds and identical resubmission follow the agreed C3 outcomes. Alias recovery survives clear/restart and is not forgotten before durable consumer acknowledgment. Queued, rejected, lost, quarantined or retry-capped mandatory evidence remains visible and blocks successful completion; an empty queue cannot erase a retained rejection. TEST-QB-009: distinguishes_confirmed_audit_from_pending_recovery. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-069: For every actual user request, including steering, the confirmed record preserves its complete request and final response text prepared for delivery, under the captured workspace, native session, MCP session and request identities, subject only to the existing secret policy and this operator-approved storage normalization: U+2013 and U+2014 become U+002D. Those two Unicode dash characters must not be stored; do not bypass the REPL normalization with escaping. After that policy, server readback is ordinally identical to the full expected text, preserving all other Unicode, Markdown, whitespace and newlines without trimming or summarization. A title or summary may be separate metadata but never substitutes for the response. Completion checks the expected request/event/result set, not only empty queues or equal counts. Missing, summarized, truncated, duplicated, misattributed or otherwise modified content blocks successful completion and remains visible for recovery. Cancellation without a final result does not invent one. Replay preserves one logical record and the same normalized full text. A crash after persistence but before delivery must not be represented as proof that the operator received the response. TEST cases: Both prohibited dash characters normalize to ASCII hyphens; literal and escaped input cannot retain prohibited dashes; existing ASCII hyphens and unrelated Unicode remain unchanged; exact whitespace/newline/Markdown response; same-count wrong request; summary substituted for result; omitted ingress event with zero pending counters; steering before/after response persistence; two sessions with identical text; timeout before/after server commit; crash before actual delivery; redaction identical on both output boundaries. TEST-QB-069: preserves_exact_request_and_final_result_with_complete_turn_coverage. TDD: P1.

    - id: FR-QB-004
      title: Enforced completion obligations
      body: >-
        ### FR-QB-004 (New): Enforced completion obligations

        TR-QB-COMPLETION-001 (New): Await a pre-completion gate for completion tools, text-only replies, success events, and final delivery; verification matches current changed state.

        - AC-QB-010: Successful final-answer payloads/success events remain withheld until required checks pass; blocked or incomplete diagnostics remain deliverable without claiming success. Test successful, correctable-incomplete and infrastructure-blocked outcomes through each final-delivery path. A corrected final attempt uses the same open request and only succeeds after every applicable obligation is verified; unchanged incomplete attempts stop at the existing bounded limit. Infrastructure failure exposes supported recovery without allowing ordinary work or discarding audit evidence. TEST-QB-010: gates_all_successful_completion_paths. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-011: Code/doc edits and command-made changes invalidate stale evidence; failed/missing applicable checks block completion. The signed policy selects every applicable runner from package ownership and dependency scope, including non-sdk VS Code suites, all distinct desktop runners and required native checks. Evidence binds policy digest and pre/post source fingerprints; changes during verification invalidate it. Ignored receipt churn alone does not invalidate source evidence. Baseline failures, blocked chains and required platform/credential cases remain explicit blockers until resolved or changed by an operator decision. TEST-QB-011: blocks_completion_on_failed_missing_or_stale_verification. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-012: A host-owned classifier derives phaseId and phaseClosing from trusted governed TODO/task mutations and MCP records, never model prose. It classifies operationClass from that trusted state plus source fingerprints: any working-tree content change within the verification-policy scope is development, whether made by an edit tool or command; administrative turns have unchanged source contents and only TODO, requirement or session-record effects. Administrative turns carry no verification or HV obligation; development turns complete only after required verification passes for the current fingerprint; a mutation completing a task or setting done: true on a TODO listed as phase-gated by the signed workspace verification policy is rejected without a valid HV receipt; for this workspace the policy lists QB-AGENT-001 tasks prefixed P1: through P5: and Final:, and done: true on QB-AGENT-001; TODOs without a phase-gate entry carry no HV obligation. The named test rejects forged reviewer/root identities, model-selected phase selectors, partial or missing verdict persistence, absent scores and every sub-98 value without rounding; it accepts valid lexical scores only under the agreed lossless numeric contract. Canonical task readback must match the attempted phase transition and current verified plan/base/head; read failure or mismatch leaves that transition pending. Administrative reconciliation never satisfies a product AC or silently closes a phase. TEST-QB-012: classifies_operations_and_gates_phase_closure_on_verified_hv_receipt (administrative, development, valid receipt, forged receipt, stale receipt). TDD: P1. Valid receipt: read back through the supported plugin from a completed MCP turn whose session agent identity is the configured reviewer identity (ClaudeCode), not the host identity; its stored verdict records OverallVerdict AGREE, accuracy and completeness >=98, and plan hash, base SHA and head SHA equal to the closing state. The host binds model-facing session tools to its own agentIdentity and sessionId; tool arguments cannot set agent, sourceType or sessionId. An administrator or unrestricted user-authorized shell with the raw marker key can bypass the application and forge server records; this on-disk credential bypass is outside the application-level guarantee and is documented as a limit under AC-QB-054.

        - AC-QB-071: Every required verification fixture and its child processes use isolated application state and explicitly selected test identities, workspace, discovery endpoints and ports before application initialization. Tests must not read live operator credentials, attach to a live operator hub or change operator application state. Seeded external-state canaries and inventories remain unchanged after success, assertion failure, timeout and cancellation. Cleanup affects only resources owned by that test run. Any intentionally live integration fixture uses an explicitly provisioned test account/workspace and cannot silently inherit the operator account. Read-only compiler/package caches may be shared when they contain no operator application identity or mutable product state. TEST cases: Pre-import environment capture; account feature-flag callback; real HOME inherited by a child; parallel fixtures; wrong discovery file/port; failure and timeout cleanup; mocked negative fixture plus a real compiled positive launch; canaries outside the test root. TEST-QB-071: isolates_all_verification_processes_from_operator_application_state. TDD: P1. Staged regressions: P2, P3, P4, P5.

        - AC-QB-018: Local hub, direct providers, compatible self-controlled remote hosts work without a Cline account. Include positive authenticated direct-provider execution, configured proxy use and compatible hub/remote operation; missing or invalid direct-provider credentials produce an actionable failure, never a Cline account fallback or silent provider substitution. TEST-QB-018: runs_permitted_execution_without_cline_account. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-061: Desktop onboarding contains no Cline account sign-in, account-key, hosted recommendation, subscription-upsell or account-backed GitHub activation path.         - AC-QB-062: A setup form offers only permitted providers whose declared authentication and required configuration it can collect.         - AC-QB-063: Empty, failed, delayed or disabled desktop schedule catalogs never synthesize an enabled provider or model. TEST-QB-063: surfaces_schedule_catalog_failure_without_fallback. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-064: Schedule creation requires an explicit permitted provider and model, or a previously explicit remembered pair still available in that same provider catalog. Missing provider/model blocks submission with an actionable message and no mutation. Editing or catalog refresh preserves the existing permitted pair, without choosing the first catalog entry or borrowing another provider model. Valid direct create/update preserves that exact pair. TEST-QB-064: preserves_explicit_schedule_provider_model_selection. TDD: P1.

        - AC-QB-065: Editing a legacy hosted schedule presents an actionable exclusion diagnostic and requires an explicit direct provider/model replacement before saving. TEST-QB-065: requires_explicit_replacement_of_hosted_schedule_selection. TDD: P1.

Missing or malformed members remain incomplete and block saving until explicitly repaired; they never inherit a provider or model from legacy scalar fields. Schedules without the structured field retain their explicit legacy direct pair. Mixed-format and partially migrated records cannot combine identities from different provider selections. TEST-QB-066: keeps_migrated_schedule_model_selection_atomic. TDD: P1.

Moving from an unavailable hosted history session to permitted execution requires an explicit new local or self-controlled remote session; it does not silently reinterpret the old session. Explicit local recovery preserves a permitted captured or remembered provider/model pair, leaves missing selection incomplete for Settings, and never chooses a hosted or first-catalog fallback. TEST-QB-067: requires_explicit_direct_desktop_recovery. TDD: P1.

      title: Safe refresh/context isolation
      body: >-
        ### FR-QB-009 (New): Safe refresh/context isolation

        TR-QB-DATA-001 (New): Context-keyed queries/invalidation, bounded visible polling, stale/cancellation handling, and backend-only credential access.

        - AC-QB-025: Both hosts use the same supported plugin read service; no direct storage reads, duplicate raw-REST client, or browser MCP secrets. TEST-QB-025: routes_panel_reads_through_shared_plugin_service. TDD: P2; host regressions P3/P4.

        - AC-QB-026: Events/reconnect/manual/configured polling refresh data without overlap; discard old-context replies; failures retain only matching-context last-good data with stale/error state. Manual refresh and events coalesce with the active request; reconnect/configuration/workspace/session changes invalidate old generations, including late successful replies after cancellation. Hiding or disposing the view stops display polling; revealing resumes in the current context. Polling bounds and default match QbrainSettings, and failed reads never become empty successes. TEST-QB-026: refreshes_without_overlaps_or_cross_context_results. TDD: P2.

        - AC-QB-027: Browsing/refresh create no model calls or agent turns; hidden stops needless display polling, not audit/enforcement. TEST-QB-027: keeps_panel_refresh_independent_of_agent_execution. TDD: P2.

        - AC-QB-074: Session Log and TODO content is displayed as data. ANSI/OSC/CSI sequences, HTML, scripts, remote resources and instruction-like text in server fields cannot execute code, alter terminal/window/clipboard state, initiate automatic network access, invoke a tool, mutate records or approve an action. Renderers safely represent such content while preserving the canonical value and existing explicit detail/copy security rules. This holds for summary, detail, error, loading-to-loaded updates and restored views in both TUI and desktop. TEST cases: OSC clipboard and hyperlink escapes; CSI cursor controls; HTML/script and remote image content; malformed Unicode; instruction-like text; status/error field injection; narrow live/restored views; explicit safe detail and copy. TEST-QB-074: renders_session_log_and_todo_content_as_inert_data. TDD: P2. Staged regressions: P3, P4.

        - AC-QB-076: A single oversized or malformed record, detail value or streamed response cannot cause unbounded transport buffering or UI work. The slice contract defines supported byte/item limits and recoverable boundary outcomes before implementation. Supported complete data remains available without silent loss; an over-limit or malformed response is explicitly failed/stale with actionable expansion or recovery behavior and is never shown as confirmed complete truncated data. Cancellation/context change releases work and prevents late rendering under another context. Ordinary navigation and governance remain responsive. TEST cases: One huge item in a small page; exact byte limit and one over; many small items; malformed encoding; endless chunk stream; cancellation midway; repeated expansion; old-context completion; full supported data remains available. TEST-QB-076: bounds_individual_record_and_detail_payload_processing. TDD: P2. Staged regressions: P3, P4.

        ### FR-QB-016 (New): Remember preferences across invocations

        TR-QB-PERSIST-001 (New): Persist panel preferences only in dedicated versioned <resolved cline-qb settings root>/cline-qb-tui.json with its own typed schema (TUI layout, visibility, dimensions and controls, the persistent-preference contract), validated field-level patches under per-file interprocess lock, atomic temp-file-plus-rename, startup restore and explicit persistence errors; never in a shared global settings file.

Concurrent processes patch different fields without losing either saved choice; explicit preference changes persist while transient fit does not. TEST-QB-047: persists_requested_preferences_not_transient_layout. TDD: P3.

        - AC-QB-048: Invalid fields recover without erasing other settings; failed saves are reported, not claimed persisted. Exercise invalid types, non-finite/fractional dimensions, malformed binding lists, corrupt/truncated files, unsupported schema versions, permission failure and interrupted saves. Preserve unrelated valid fields and recoverable original content; do not silently rewrite an unsupported version as successfully migrated. The user can recover/reset through the existing settings path. TEST-QB-048: handles_corrupt_preferences_and_failed_saves_honestly. TDD: P3.

        - AC-QB-075: After a preference writer terminates unexpectedly at any persistence step, a new invocation can read a complete valid old or new document and make a subsequent valid save within the slice contract recovery bound, without manual deletion of abandoned coordination state. Recovery cannot steal a live writer ownership or discard unrelated valid fields. If the environment prevents recovery, report the unsaved state and keep usable last-good presentation instead of hanging or claiming persistence. The recovery bound and writer-ownership outcomes are fixed before implementation; no particular locking mechanism is prescribed. TEST cases: Kill before temporary write, during write, before/after replacement and while holding any coordination resource; restart then save; concurrent live writer; permission failure; unrelated-field preservation; bounded failure diagnostic. TEST-QB-075: recovers_preference_write_progress_after_writer_failure. TDD: P3.

Generic SDK defaults remain compatible through host injection. P1 establishes the runtime isolation cases; P5 owns final all-host branding, compatibility and installed-artifact acceptance.     - id: TR-MCP-DB-006
      title: Concurrent turn deletes serialized per session
      body: >-
        Concurrent sessionlog_delete_turn operations on a single session SHALL be serialized through a process-wide per-session gate so a burst (observed: 13 parallel deletes) cannot exhaust or poison the SQL Server connection pool; deletes on different sessions SHALL still run concurrently; the deployed SqlClient ConnectRetryCount=6/ConnectRetryInterval=10s defaults SHALL be preserved. Acceptance Criteria: (AC1) acquiring the per-session lock for the same key blocks a second acquirer until release, while a different key acquires without blocking (KeyedAsyncLock); (AC2) DeleteTurnAsync continues to soft-delete a turn and refresh the parent turn count correctly under the lock. Origin: BUG-TRIAGE-079 (concurrent gated deletes poisoned the pool with SqlClient error 19 then 40 for ~3 minutes while SQL Server stayed up). Note: pool poisoning is a SQL-Server-runtime property not unit-reproducible; the deterministic serialization proof is the KeyedAsyncLock unit test, with SessionLogService.DeleteTurnAsync wrapped in the per-session lock keyed by sourceType/sessionId. Validated by TEST-MCP-DB-006.

        **Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-105; TEST: TEST-MCP-138, TEST-MCP-139, TEST-MCP-140, TEST-MCP-DB-006

    - id: TR-MCP-HEALTH-003
      title: Health reflects storage reachability and backend errors are typed
      body: >-
        Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-096. GET /health is liveness-only (tags live: self plus FederationUpstreamHealthCheck) with no storage connectivity check, so when the database backend is unreachable the server still answers Healthy and echoes the trust nonce correctly while every persistence call fails. Observed live on 2026-07-20 when the SQL host was powered off: marker trust passed, then todo_list returned a raw SqlClient "Named Pipes Provider, error: 40" string, sessionlog_query returned a misleading "transient failure, consider EnableRetryOnFailure" hint, triage_report returned a bare "an error occurred", and the plugin wrapper returned an opaque 30-second timeout, so no caller could tell that storage was simply down. The server SHALL expose storage reachability on the health path, either by degrading the status or by an explicit storage field, WITHOUT breaking the nonce echo that marker trust bootstrap depends on. Backend-unavailable conditions SHALL surface as one typed error consistently across REST and the MCP tools, distinguishable from a malformed request. Coverage SHALL simulate an unreachable store and assert the misleading Healthy result before the fix.

        **Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-143; TEST: TEST-MCP-194, TEST-MCP-REPL-040

      priority: medium

Node reuse keeps such a node alive after the build, so EOF never arrives; when an idle reusable node already exists the build connects to it instead and nothing inherits the pipes, which explains the earlier passing run. Provenance: in every experiment the node's parent PID, read while the build child ran, was the child. Mechanism: dotnet test sets MSBUILDENSURESTDOUTFORTASKPROCESSES=1 for vstest.console, the test host, and the test executable (the dotnet test process itself has it unset), so every build a Build.Tests case starts inherits it. With it set, MSBuild starts worker nodes without redirecting their standard streams, and a node spawned by the build inherits the build's redirected stdout and stderr (the output stayed open 30 s after exit). Without it, as from a plain shell, the node gets its own streams and the output closes at once. Node reuse keeps the node alive after the build.       body: >-
        Implements FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002. OllamaServerController lives in tests/TestSupport.Shared with no xunit dependency; its probe delegate, executable resolver, process launcher, poll interval, timeout, delay, and clock are injected so the policy is unit-testable without a real Ollama binary. It is linked into McpServer.Support.Mcp.Tests and McpServer.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests through tests/Directory.Build.targets following the Validation.Shared linked-source idiom. EnsureRunningAsync probes first, launches only when the probe fails, then polls until the probe succeeds or the timeout elapses; on timeout it terminates any process it started before throwing. A resolver returning no executable throws an InvalidOperationException naming the InstallOllama Nuke target without attempting a launch.     - id: TR-MCP-REPL-016
      title: Failsafe queue drains oldest-first after a proven-reachable backend call
      body: >-
        BUG-TRIAGE-097. The plugin PowerShell runtime captures every session-log submit into the failsafe queue before the remote call but never replays it, so records accumulate forever (33 on disk in F:/GitHub/McpServer, oldest 2026-07-14). plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST expose Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, which walks the failsafe directory oldest-first (the file name is prefixed with the UTC capture stamp, so a name sort is a chronological sort) and re-issues each record's captured method and params through Invoke-ReplRaw. A record MUST be deleted only after its submission succeeds; a record whose submission fails MUST stay on disk. client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync is an upsert keyed by sessionId plus requestId, so a replay is idempotent. A record rejected by the backend MUST NOT block the newer records behind it: the drain increments that record's drainAttempts counter and continues the walk. A transport-level failure (MCP_UNTRUSTED, mcpserver-repl not on PATH, timeout, refused connection) MUST abort the pass without consuming any attempt budget, because the backend and not the record is at fault. The drain MUST skip the record belonging to the submit currently in flight, so a drain triggered inside an active submit cannot double-submit or delete the live turn. The drain MUST be wired to the first successful Invoke-ReplRaw in the process (Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccess, latched to run at most once and disabled by MCP_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_DISABLED=1) rather than to bootstrap: bootstrap only proves the marker file is fresh, does not prove the backend answers, and runs inside Invoke-ReplRaw, so draining there would recurse. Operators MUST be able to force a full pass with the plugin-local verb workflow.failsafe.drain (optional maxRecords and maxAttempts params), which prints the drain summary as YAML and exits non-zero only when the pass aborted.

    - id: TR-MCP-SEC-006
      title: Brain-slot signing keys follow a renamed party id
      body: "CORRECTED 2026-07-20 after the original specification was proven wrong by test. Context unchanged: trusted parties and their keys live in the TransactionSecurity key store (KeyServerPartyEntity, KeyServerPartyKeyEntity), a separate SQLite database created with EnsureCreated, so the McpDbContext Creativity/Logic rename migration cannot reach them; BrainSlotRegistryService.RegisterPartyAsync registers the party only and never a key, while ValidateReadinessAsync requires an active signing key at \"{partyId}:signing:1\". On any migrated installation the renamed party therefore starts with no key and the quad reports NotReady. WHAT WAS WRONG: the first version of this requirement said to COPY the legacy party's signing key material forward. That is impossible and harmful. PartyKeyDescriptor and KeyServerPartyKeyEntity expose only PublicKeyPem, so only the public half can ever be read; InMemoryKeyServerService retains a private ECDsa handle only for a pair it generated itself, and CreateSigningKey given a public PEM with no private PEM stores an empty private-key set. The result passed every readiness gate and could never sign: turn transactions were rejected with TransactionFailureReason.UnknownKey after the model provider had already been invoked and billed, and persisting that row also suppressed TurnTransactionCoordinator.EnsureDefaultPartiesAsync, which mints a working pair only when no key row exists. CORRECT BEHAVIOR: when a brain slot's party has no active signing key and a legacy party id exists (brain-slot:left-hemisphere for Creativity, brain-slot:right-hemisphere for Logic), the runtime SHALL register the renamed party with NO key material so the keyserver mints a fresh pair and retains its private half, and SHALL leave the legacy party and key rows untouched. Historical verification is unaffected because a manifest carries its own PublisherPartyId and VerifyManifestAsync resolves the public key from that legacy party. Reconciliation remains idempotent, is a no-op when the new key already exists or no legacy party is found, and never rotates an existing key. Proven by TEST-MCP-192 and by BrainSlotAdoptedPartyKeySigningTests, which now assert a committed turn transaction under the renamed party and continued verification of a legacy-signed manifest."

      - id: AC-001
        text: On Linux with Landlock, a missing export root (with its missing ancestors) and missing nested export folders are created on a thread Landlock-confined to the pinned root or, for a missing root, its deepest existing ancestor (pinned from its approved mount without following links or crossing mounts); a parent moved outside before mkdirat is refused by the kernel and nothing appears outside (BUG-BASELINE-001; BugTriage139EighteenthLinuxTests EnsureDirectory_MissingNestedDirectory_IsCreatedUnderLandlock, EnsureDirectory_ParentMovedOutsideBeforeCreate_IsDeniedByLandlock, OpenExportRoot_MissingRootAndAncestors_IsCreatedUnderLandlock, LandlockConfinement_DeniesDirectoryCreationOutsideItsHierarchy).
        isSatisfied: false

        text: On Linux with Landlock, nested stale files and empty directories are deleted on a thread Landlock-confined to the root through the pinned parent after the target kind and identity match; a missing parent or target returns false; a parent moved outside before unlinkat is refused by the kernel and the entry survives; export cleanup deletes nested stale files (BUG-BASELINE-001; DeleteFileIfExists_NestedStaleFile_DeletesUnderLandlock, DeleteFileIfExists_NestedParentMovedOutsideBeforeUnlink_IsDeniedByLandlock, RequirementsExport_NestedStaleCleanup_DeletesStaleUnderLandlock).

        text: 'On Linux without Landlock the export fails closed as before: missing roots and nested folders throw DirectoryNotFoundException before any mutation and nested stale cleanup is refused before any generated write (BUG-BASELINE-001; EnsureDirectory_MissingNestedDirectory_FailsClosedBeforeMutation, OpenExportRoot_MissingRoot_FailsClosedWithoutLandlock, RequirementsExport_NestedStaleCleanup_IsRejectedBeforeGeneratedWrite).'

One explicit decision has the same identity and conclusion in designDecisions, decision dialog and design_decision action after replay; tool activity alone does not invent a decision.       - id: AC-QB-009
        text: 'AC-QB-009: Pending/synthetic acknowledgments are not confirmed persistence; recovery retains records and avoids duplicate application. Crash/restart at capture, pending-to-minted rebinding, submission, server commit, receipt handling and retirement retains immutable event identity, payload and per-turn order. At-least-once replay applies one logical event and never changes its request attribution. Confirmed and verified-unchanged receipts require matching root identities, event/payload and positive committed revision; duplicate requestIds and identical resubmission follow the agreed C3 outcomes. Alias recovery survives clear/restart and is not forgotten before durable consumer acknowledgment. Queued, rejected, lost, quarantined or retry-capped mandatory evidence remains visible and blocks successful completion; an empty queue cannot erase a retained rejection. TEST-QB-009: distinguishes_confirmed_audit_from_pending_recovery. TDD: P1.'
        isSatisfied: false
      - id: AC-QB-069
        text: 'AC-QB-069: For every actual user request, including steering, the confirmed record preserves its complete request and final response text prepared for delivery, under the captured workspace, native session, MCP session and request identities, subject only to the existing secret policy and this operator-approved storage normalization: U+2013 and U+2014 become U+002D. Those two Unicode dash characters must not be stored; do not bypass the REPL normalization with escaping. After that policy, server readback is ordinally identical to the full expected text, preserving all other Unicode, Markdown, whitespace and newlines without trimming or summarization. A title or summary may be separate metadata but never substitutes for the response. Completion checks the expected request/event/result set, not only empty queues or equal counts. Missing, summarized, truncated, duplicated, misattributed or otherwise modified content blocks successful completion and remains visible for recovery. Cancellation without a final result does not invent one. Replay preserves one logical record and the same normalized full text. A crash after persistence but before delivery must not be represented as proof that the operator received the response. TEST cases: Both prohibited dash characters normalize to ASCII hyphens; literal and escaped input cannot retain prohibited dashes; existing ASCII hyphens and unrelated Unicode remain unchanged; exact whitespace/newline/Markdown response; same-count wrong request; summary substituted for result; omitted ingress event with zero pending counters; steering before/after response persistence; two sessions with identical text; timeout before/after server commit; crash before actual delivery; redaction identical on both output boundaries. TEST-QB-069: preserves_exact_request_and_final_result_with_complete_turn_coverage. TDD: P1.'
        isSatisfied: false

Administrative turns carry no verification or HV obligation; development turns complete only after required verification passes for the current fingerprint; a mutation completing a task or setting done: true on a TODO listed as phase-gated by the signed workspace verification policy is rejected without a valid HV receipt; for this workspace the policy lists QB-AGENT-001 tasks prefixed P1: through P5: and Final:, and done: true on QB-AGENT-001; TODOs without a phase-gate entry carry no HV obligation.         designDecisions:
        - 'All-docs scope recorded from the operator ruling (latest ruling governs over the 2026-10-11 ruling that required Mermaid activity diagrams per unit of work). Consequence: 435 Mermaid fences in 4 docs, 4 .mmd files in docs/Marketing/diagrams, and 21 .mmd files in PR 84 are in scope; docs/receipts (8 fences, 3 .mmd) is proposed out of scope because receipts are historical evidence.'
        - 'Non-C4 diagram kinds can be native: structurizr/cli:2025.11.09 validated a probe DSL using custom elements with Activity, Decision (Diamond shape), Entity and State tags, groups, custom views and a dynamic view (exit 0). Consequence: the recommended mapping keeps every diagram inside one workspace definition with no second diagram language as source.'
        - 'Rendering for markdown is a build activity: docs need committed images generated from the workspace; that is a Nuke target (TR-MCP-NUKE-* under FR-MCP-BUILD-001), which falls under the standing code freeze. Consequence: the operator decides on an exemption before build code is written.'
        - 'The two SessionTurn architecture docs (320 fences) belong to an HV effort that is still open (Amendment 1 last remediated 2026-10-18T04:23 before round 5). Consequence: converting their diagrams changes HV-reviewed artifacts and requires a new HV of architecture and plan; sequencing is an operator decision.'
        - 'Requirement changes go through plan approval (profile 4.3): converting the Quad-Model doc breaks TEST-MCP-165 as written (TurnTransactionPlanArtifactTests asserts six Mermaid fences), so TR-MCP-TXNDIAGRAMS-001 and TEST-MCP-165 need reconciled text. Consequence: the new TR was captured now; the existing records stay unchanged until the operator approves the proposed text.'
        - 'Product test code is outside the granted exemption: rewriting tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests/Documentation/TurnTransactionPlanArtifactTests.cs is product test code under the code freeze, while the exemption covered only the Nuke target. Consequence: asked as a separate approval item.'
        - 'Raw Chromium screenshots of the static viewer are not acceptable renders: the 09:53 probe selected the right views by URL hash but showed the help dialog, the dark theme and a render-time stamp. Consequence: TR-MCP-NUKE-017 AC-2 requires driving the viewer (dialog dismissed, light theme, fitted, no stamp) and saving its SVG export, byte-identical across runs.'
        - 'Out of scope by reason: docs/receipts (historical HV evidence), the product use-case Mermaid and PlantUML export features (FR-MCP-USECASE-005, -013, -014), and tools/powershell/McpContext.USER.html (an export of a markdown file with no diagram). Consequence: the AC-3 Mermaid check excludes only docs/receipts; product code that emits Mermaid is not a doc and is not scanned as a fence.'
        - 'Kept the existing deferral clause of TR-MCP-TXNDIAGRAMS-001 while applying the approved text: my proposal had omitted it because I proposed without reading the full record. Consequence: the requirement keeps "future quad-model, Curiosity, AoT, and weight-update branches SHALL remain explicitly deferred" and its Covered-by line gains the workspace; disclosed in the plan and to the operator.'
        - 'AC-6 depends on TR-MCP-NUKE-005, which is not implemented (PLAN-BUILDWHATIF-001 is a draft): presented to the operator, who chose a target-level WhatIf Nuke parameter with the name PLAN-BUILDWHATIF-001 defines. Consequence: no second dry-run mechanism; build.ps1 pass-through stays with TR-MCP-NUKE-005.'
        - 'AC-5 is measured on the rendered SVG (viewBox and text font sizes), because Structurizr lays views out on large paper-sized canvases where raw style sizes say nothing about printed size. Consequence: pass when one scale puts every text size in 10.67..16 px and the scaled viewBox fits a letter page; default styles (16.8 to 36 px) fail, so the workspace sets font sizes.'
        - 'Render determinism uses the supported switch, not SVG post-processing: with "structurizr.metadata" "false" the export is byte-identical across two Chromium runs; with metadata on it carries a hidden date line. Consequence: the workspace sets the view-set property and AC-2 needs no normalizer.'
        - 'AC-3 fence scan covers markdown only (.md, .markdown); .mmd covers all tracked files; docs/receipts excluded. Consequence: test fixtures holding fence text in C# string literals are not false positives.'
        - 'BDPv4 seam for pure rules: contract-derived fixtures and assertions are shared by a scripted mock, wrong mocks and production, so the mock gate proves the assertions before production code exists. Consequence: production binding reuses the exact assertions; no weakening is possible without editing the shared contract.'
        - 'The runner stops after a failed validation (only the Mermaid check still runs) and skips rendering on inspection errors while still checking committed renders. Consequence: findings never rest on untrustworthy view keys, and inspection errors cannot be hidden by a fresh render.'
        - 'The tooling never writes under docs during validation or export: it copies the workspace sources (excluding rendered, static, json) to a temporary directory per call. Consequence: a --what-if run changes nothing in the tree.'
        - 'The pre-existing Build.Tests failure is outside this plan and under the code freeze. Consequence: triaged; the full-suite gate needs an operator baseline exception (1 of 409) rather than a fix in this plan.'
        - 'Product unit tests run only through ./build.ps1 Test, with --test-run-id so every project writes TRX evidence. Consequence: no raw dotnet test evidence for product tests; Build.Tests stays the one direct-run exception.'
        - 'No competing fixes for code another live effort is changing: PR 83 already edits the tests of 3 failures and PR 82 edits WorkspacePathNormalizer for a fourth. Consequence: this plan fixes the other 10 and takes those 4 by merging develop after PR 82 and PR 83 land; P5 cannot close before then.'
        - 'Receipt logs are force-added despite the *.log ignore rule, following the 3 receipts already tracked that way, and a receipts README records each run including the void run and the AC-5 order deviation. Consequence: the BDPv4 chronology is reviewable from the branch.'
        - 'Retries only follow a container start: an endpoint the build did not just start gets one TCP probe, a just-started one gets up to 30 one-second probes. Consequence: an already-down endpoint fails InstallTestDependencies immediately with its host:port, while a cold container gets time to accept connections.'
        - 'Host and port are read with DbConnectionStringBuilder, not provider packages: the build project needs no Npgsql or SqlClient reference, and LocalDB is rejected by name because it has no TCP endpoint on Linux.'
        - 'The Decompose4nf SQLite failure is presented, not fixed: it is outside the 14 failures the operator ruled on, it surfaced only because Linux provisioning lets the Integration category run, and it is the legacy-key class that PR 83 (workspace rekey) owns for the RemoveTodoRecords tests. Consequence: the P5 MigrationIntegrationTests gate stays red until the operator chooses the fix.'
